rubric.why: Identifies the organisms in a species as similar or belonging to the same kind.
rubric.description: States that members of a species are similar organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying members as similar organisms of the same kind.

rubric.why: Interbreeding that produces fertile offspring is the key biological criterion in the definition.
rubric.description: States that members can interbreed and produce fertile offspring.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both interbreeding and fertile offspring.

modelAnswer: A species is a group of similar organisms that can interbreed naturally.

items.followUp: How does biodiversity help maintain ecosystem stability?

rubric.why: Qualitative observations describe characteristics rather than expressing them as measurements or counts.
rubric.description: Explains that qualitative observations describe qualities or characteristics without numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying them as descriptive or non-numerical.

rubric.why: Quantitative observations use measurements or counts and are expressed numerically.
rubric.description: Explains that quantitative observations involve measurements or counts expressed as numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying numerical measurements or counts.

modelAnswer: Qualitative observations describe qualities or characteristics without using numbers.
Quantitative observations involve measurements or counts and are expressed numerically.

items.followUp: State two observations that led A. F. A. King to associate mosquitoes with malaria.

rubric.why: King noted an association between malaria and places where mosquitoes were common, such as marshy areas.
rubric.description: Gives the observation that malaria was common in places with many mosquitoes, such as marshy areas.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid observation linking malaria occurrence with mosquitoes or their breeding places.

rubric.why: Observations about avoiding mosquito bites or exposure supported the proposed link.
rubric.description: Gives an observation that protection from mosquitoes was associated with reduced malaria.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid observation about protection from mosquitoes and lower malaria risk.

modelAnswer: Malaria was common in marshy places where mosquitoes were abundant.
People protected from mosquito bites, for example by mosquito nets or screened rooms, were less likely to get malaria.

items.followUp: State two ways biodiversity supports ecosystem balance.

rubric.why: Biodiversity helps ecosystems remain balanced and stable.
rubric.description: States that biodiversity contributes to ecosystem balance or stability.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking biodiversity with ecosystem stability or balance.

rubric.why: Different species contribute to ecosystem processes and interactions.
rubric.description: Identifies a role such as supporting food webs, nutrient cycling, or different ecological roles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid ecosystem function supported by biodiversity.

modelAnswer: Biodiversity helps maintain the balance and stability of an ecosystem.
Different species support food chains and food webs and contribute to processes such as nutrient cycling.

items.followUp: What happens to a cell placed in a hypotonic solution?

rubric.why: A hypotonic solution has a lower solute concentration than the cell, so water tends to enter the cell.
rubric.description: Defines a hypotonic solution relative to the cell as having lower solute concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the solution is less concentrated than the cell or that water enters the cell.

rubric.why: A hypertonic solution has a higher solute concentration than the cell, so water tends to leave the cell.
rubric.description: Defines a hypertonic solution relative to the cell as having higher solute concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the solution is more concentrated than the cell or that water leaves the cell.

modelAnswer: A hypotonic solution has a lower solute concentration than the cell; water moves into the cell.
A hypertonic solution has a higher solute concentration than the cell; water moves out of the cell.

items.followUp: What is the function of chloroplasts and leucoplasts?

rubric.why: Chromoplasts contain coloured pigments other than chlorophyll and give colour to plant parts.
rubric.description: Defines a chromoplast by its coloured pigments or role in colouring plant parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying chromoplasts as pigment-containing plastids that impart colour.

rubric.why: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids commonly involved in storing food.
rubric.description: Defines a leucoplast as a colourless plastid, typically used for food storage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying leucoplasts as colourless plastids or stating their storage role.

modelAnswer: Chromoplasts are plastids containing coloured pigments other than chlorophyll, which give colour to plant parts.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that commonly store food.

items.followUp: State two activities that occur in a cell during the S phase.

rubric.why: The cell grows during G1 in preparation for later stages of the cell cycle.
rubric.description: States that the cell grows during G1 phase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for cell growth or an increase in cell size.

rubric.why: G1 includes normal cellular activity and production of materials and organelles needed for growth and division.
rubric.description: States one further G1 activity, such as synthesis of proteins or organelles, or normal metabolism.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid activity other than growth.

modelAnswer: During G1 phase, the cell grows and increases in size.
It carries out normal metabolism and synthesizes proteins and organelles.

items.followUp: Describe how cytokinesis differs in animal and plant cells.

rubric.why: Animal-cell cytokinesis occurs by an inward-growing cleavage furrow that divides the cytoplasm.
rubric.description: Shows or describes the cleavage furrow in an animal cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a clearly labelled or described animal-cell cleavage furrow.

rubric.why: Plant-cell cytokinesis occurs by formation of a cell plate between the two daughter cells.
rubric.description: Shows or describes the cell plate in a plant cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a clearly labelled or described plant-cell cell plate.

modelAnswer: Animal cell: the cell membrane pinches inward to form a cleavage furrow, which divides the cytoplasm.
Plant cell: a cell plate forms in the middle and grows outward until it joins the cell wall, dividing the cytoplasm.
